entries.description:
An object of another program, reached by its name in the Windows registry (a ProgID such as "ADODB.Connection" or a fiscal register driver's). Its properties and methods are looked up when they are used, so nothing about the object has to be known when the module is compiled.

WINDOWS ONLY. The type exists on every platform, so a module that creates one compiles on macOS and Linux too; there `New COMObject` is refused when it runs, with "COM objects are available on Windows only". On Windows it works in the thin client and on the application server.

VALUES CROSS BOTH WAYS by kind: a number goes as an integer when it is one, as a double otherwise - as a DECIMAL when it has more digits than a double keeps - and comes back exactly, CY and DECIMAL included; a string, a boolean, a date, Null and Undefined go as themselves; an Array goes as an array of VARIANTs - rows of one length as one array of as many dimensions, the table a spreadsheet takes; a COMSafeArray goes as itself, with its element type and bounds; BinaryData goes as an array of bytes; another COM object goes as itself. AN ARRAY COMES BACK AS A COMSafeArray, always - `Unload()` gives it as an Array. A value with no COM spelling - a reference, a structure - is refused with its type named.

AN ARGUMENT the member declares as an output is written back into the caller's variable. An object that does not describe its members gets every argument by reference, as VBScript passes it, and a variable the member changed takes the new value. An argument left out (`Obj.Method(a, , c)`) is sent as missing, so the object uses its own default.

FOR EACH walks a collection the object exposes (ADO `Fields`, MSXML node lists, the keys of `Scripting.Dictionary`).

A FAILED CALL is raised with the object and the member named, and the object's own description of what went wrong.
entries.parameters: progId - the name the class is registered under. One that is not registered is refused, and the message names it.

entries.description:
Calls `handler` each time the object raises the event `eventName`. The events are those of the object's default event interface; an object that has none, or no event by that name, is refused.

The handler receives the event's arguments in order, as many of them as it declares - the rule a form's event handler is called by; an argument the object passes by reference takes the value the handler left in it.

An event is handled on the thread that owns the object: while the script is inside a call to the object, or, in the thin client, whenever it is idle. A handler that raises an error raises it from the call during which the event came.
entries.parameters:
eventName - the event's name, as the object declares it.
handler - a function: `Function(arg1, arg2) { ... }`; or the name of a procedure of the module that subscribes (`New Event("Name")` is taken too), called through that module. An unknown name is refused at once.

entries.description: Stops calling the handler given for `eventName`. When no handler is left the platform disconnects from the object's events.

entries.signature: New COMSafeArray(elementType : string, size1 : number [, ..., sizeN : number])    New COMSafeArray(values : Array, elementType : string [, size1 : number, ..., sizeN : number])    New COMSafeArray(source : COMSafeArray)
entries.description:
An array as COM holds it (a SAFEARRAY): elements of one type, as many dimensions as it was made with, each with its own lower bound. It is what a COM method declaring an array of a type - `SAFEARRAY(long)`, `SAFEARRAY(BSTR)` - takes, and what a spreadsheet's `Range.Value` gives back, counted from 1.

AN ARRAY A COM OBJECT RETURNS IS ALWAYS A COMSafeArray - a method's result, a property, an output argument, an event's argument - kept as it came. `Unload()` gives it as an Array.

TO A COM METHOD it goes as itself, with its element type and bounds. An Array goes by itself too, as VARIANTs; a COMSafeArray is for a method that wants another element type or other bounds.

DIMENSIONS are numbered from 0, the first dimension being the one the first index walks (the rows of a spreadsheet's range). AN INDEX is the array's own, from its lower bound to its upper one.

WINDOWS ONLY, as COMObject: the type exists on every platform, and `New` is refused elsewhere.
entries.parameters:
elementType - automation's name of the element type: "VT_I1", "VT_I2", "VT_I4", "VT_I8", "VT_UI1", "VT_UI2", "VT_UI4", "VT_UI8", "VT_INT", "VT_UINT", "VT_R4", "VT_R8", "VT_CY", "VT_DECIMAL", "VT_DATE", "VT_BSTR", "VT_BOOL", "VT_ERROR", "VT_VARIANT", "VT_DISPATCH", "VT_UNKNOWN". Another name is refused.
size1, ..., sizeN - the number of elements of each dimension, the first first; or one Array of them. Every dimension starts at 0, and every element is its type's empty one.
values - an Array of the elements: arrays in arrays, as deep as there are dimensions. Without sizes it is taken in its own shape - rows of one length make one more dimension; with them it must have exactly that shape.
source - a COMSafeArray to copy.

entries.description: The number of the array's dimensions.
The number of elements of a dimension.
entries.parameters: dimension - from 0, the first dimension first. One the array does not have is refused.

entries.description: The index a dimension starts at: 0 for an array made in the module, 1 for a spreadsheet's range.
entries.parameters: dimension - from 0, the first dimension first. One the array does not have is refused.

entries.description: The index a dimension ends at: its lower bound plus its length, less one.
entries.parameters: dimension - from 0, the first dimension first. One the array does not have is refused.

entries.description: The element type, by automation's name: "VT_I4", "VT_BSTR", "VT_VARIANT" and so on.
entries.example: Message(Data.GetType());              // VT_VARIANT for a spreadsheet's range

entries.description: The element at the indices, one for each dimension, the first dimension first. An index is the array's own, from its lower bound; one outside the bounds is refused with "Index goes beyond array", and so is a call with another number of indices. An element that is an array itself is a COMSafeArray.
entries.parameters: index1, ..., indexN - the element's index in each dimension.
entries.example: Value = Data.GetValue(1, 2);          // row 1, column 2 of a range

entries.signature: Arr.SetValue(index1 : number, ..., indexN : number, value : any)
entries.description: Puts the value at the indices. A value of another kind is changed to the element type the way automation changes one - 13.5 into a VT_I4 is 14, the text "12" into a VT_R8 is 12 - and one that cannot be is refused, with the element type named.
entries.parameters:
index1, ..., indexN - the element's index in each dimension, as in GetValue.
value - what to put there.

entries.description: Whether Resize can change the array: an array made in the module can; one whose size the COM object fixed cannot.
Changes the number of elements of the LAST dimension - the only one a COM array can change. The elements already there keep their places; new ones are their type's empty one.
entries.parameters: size - the new number of elements of the last dimension, 0 or more.
entries.example:
var Table = New COMSafeArray("VT_VARIANT", 2, 3);
Table.Resize(5);                      // 2 rows of 5

entries.description: The elements as an Array: arrays in arrays, the first dimension the outermost - for a spreadsheet's range, an Array of rows, each an Array of the row's values.
